protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: NOT CONFIRMED. The advisory and PR assert only a potential XSS from using URIUtil.addPaths instead of addEncodedPaths. At the claimed 2013 introducer and CVE-listed Release_1.92, Jetty 9.0.5/9.2.19 documents and implements addPaths as the encoded-path combiner; it does not decode request.getRequestURI(). In both those versions and Jetty 9.4.52, Resource.getListHTML passes the base through hrefEncodeURI, which percent-encodes double quote, single quote, less-than, and greater-than before emitting href attributes, while the decoded title and entry labels are de-tagged. No advisory reference supplies a request/response PoC or demonstrates an escaping bypass.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: FAILED. 4b77733e59dd8af742ff826c90c8d40b542b7563 first wrote the YaCy call, but with Jetty 9.0.5 that call selected the correct encoded-path API, so it did not first write the alleged addPaths-versus-addEncodedPaths flaw. YaCy commit e6e20dab5279900a9929dd6935cac97b48bef249 later upgraded Jetty 9.2.21 to 9.4.6 while retaining the call; Jetty 9.4.6 had split the old behavior into addEncodedPaths and redefined addPaths for decoded paths. That dependency transition is a candidate origin only, not a confirmed BIC, because exploitability is still unproved.

protocol_checks.bic_only_ai_attribution: UNRESOLVED. The claimed 4b77733e59dd8af742ff826c90c8d40b542b7563 object has human author/committer reger and no AI/bot/co-author trailer, but it is not a valid BIC for the alleged API-semantic flaw. The dependency-transition candidate e6e20dab5279900a9929dd6935cac97b48bef249 likewise has human author/committer reger and no AI marker, but BIC-only attribution cannot be closed until the vulnerability and its actual BIC are established. Fix-side authorship was not used.

findings: The primary record's central statement that addPaths failed to keep request-URI characters encoded in 2013 is contradicted by the exact Jetty 9.0.5 and 9.2.x API contract: at that time addPaths was the encoded-path combiner later renamed addEncodedPaths.

The claimed BIC predates the only identified YaCy-side semantic transition by nearly four years; e6e20dab5279900a9929dd6935cac97b48bef249 is not an ancestor of Release_1.92 but is an ancestor of Release_1.940 and Release_1.941.

The sink has explicit dangerous-character encoding, and neither the CNA record nor PR 722 demonstrates a payload that bypasses it. A published, non-withdrawn advisory is not sufficient mechanism evidence.

Because the actual vulnerability is unresolved, the primary NOT_AI verdict cannot be confirmed even though both the rejected introducer and the dependency-transition candidate have human-only commit objects.
remaining_gap: Provide a reproducible raw HTTP request against an affected YaCy build that reaches an enabled directory listing and produces executable script in the returned HTML, including the exact requestURI value after Jetty parsing and the generated getListHTML output. Then reconcile why the CNA range ends at Release_1.92 although the proposed API-semantic transition first enters YaCy at e6e20dab5279900a9929dd6935cac97b48bef249 and Release_1.940 retains the allegedly vulnerable call. Only after that can the atomic BIC, affected releases, advisory validity, and BIC-only AI verdict be closed.
